page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It features 32 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this server in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35. In memory-intensive tasks, it registers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1705.41 GB/sec, which drops to 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and vector instruction capabilities, such as AVX-512 and AES, assist in processing tasks like bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 140.98 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 28.91 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio of 1:4, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without the premium of memory-optimized configurations. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage means all storage operations must traverse the network, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy applications. Additionally, the absence of GPU acceleration limits its utility for large-scale machine learning, though it can handle smaller LLM inference tasks, achieving 12.4 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

This server is suited for general-purpose enterprise applications, multi-threaded compilation tasks, static web serving, and medium-scale database operations. Its dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed also make it appropriate for moderate computational tasks, such as text and image processing, where consistent CPU performance is required.
